commit_reviews.summary: Incremental build feature lands as a clean, well-tested extension of the existing generator architecture—`incremental.ts`/`cache.ts` mirror `generator.ts` conventions, `BuildStats` slots into `types.ts`, exports flow through `index.ts`, and the 469-line test mirrors `generator.test.ts` patterns exactly.

compounding_issues: Session 4's SSG class + plugin lifecycle architecture (ssg.ts, plugin.ts, plugins/*, ssg.config.ts) is dead code — nothing ever calls new SSG(), loadFromConfig(), or wires plugins into the CLI; the build path still uses parseMarkdownFiles + generateSite directly, leaving two parallel architectures where session 5 built on the old function-based pipeline instead of the new one
dist/ build artifacts were committed in sessions 3 and 4, then deleted in session 5 — avoidable repo-hygiene churn that inflates every intervening diff
generateSiteIncremental duplicates generator.ts rendering logic (own renderPage/renderLayout loop) rather than composing with the existing generateSite, spreading rendering logic across three modules
SSG.serve() in session 4 is an incomplete stub — it fires onStart/onEnd plugin hooks but never actually starts a server, an unfinished abstraction shipped into the refactor
key_decisions: Session 1 replaced the Todo-API seed with a clean function-based pipeline (parser → generator → CLI) plus Jest/ts-jest strict-mode TypeScript baseline
Session 2 extracted a TemplateEngine backed by Handlebars with .hbs layouts/partials, replacing inline HTML string building in generator.ts
Session 3 added a dev server (server.ts) with WebSocket live-reload and chokidar file watching, wired into the CLI as a serve subcommand

Session 4 introduced a plugin abstraction (Plugin interface with onStart/beforeBuild/onFile/afterBuild/onEnd hooks) and config-file loading — architecturally ambitious but never connected to the CLI entry point
Session 5 added a content-hash based incremental build cache (CacheManager + .ssg-cache.json manifest) with --incremental/--clean CLI flags and a large test suite
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality improved across the sessions: the greenfield baseline grew into a feature-complete SSG with templating, a live-reload dev server, config support, and incremental builds, with test coverage expanding in lockstep (parser, generator, templates, cli, server, incremental all tested; 878 lines of tests at HEAD) and strict TypeScript throughout. However the arc is not smooth — session 4's refactor added a sophisticated plugin architecture that was never adopted by the code paths sessions 3 and 5 actually exercised, so the trajectory is two-track: the working pipeline matured steadily while the abstracted rewrite remained disconnected, and session 5's cross-cutting work reinforced the older path rather than consolidating the two.
story_review.summary: A logical session arc with steadily growing features and tests, undermined by session 4 shipping an unintegrated plugin architecture that sessions 3 and 5's CLI pipeline never used.
